attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post; he quotes the Stanford paper separately, but this sentence is his own assessment.

semantics.note: Faithful restatement: the study reinforces Nguyen's long-running findings, with the named paper title kept and 'underappreciated' retained as his aside.

contract.note: Reading 'reinforces' as substantive corroboration of a shared conclusion, not replication, is the ordinary reading. Leaving 'underappreciated' out of the verdict is reasonable.

evidence.note: MIRAGE v2 (26 Mar 2026, before the post) concludes high benchmark accuracy does not reliably indicate visual understanding.
Nguyen-coauthored named paper (v1 Jul 2024, v6 Mar 2025) finds VLMs score high on benchmarks yet fail simple visual tasks.
v1 (May 2025) of a second Nguyen-coauthored paper documents VLM visual failures driven by prior knowledge; supports 'series of papers'.

reviews.rationale: Both the new study and Nguyen's earlier papers conclude that strong benchmark performance overstates VLMs' visual understanding. The methods differ: the new study tests without images, while BlindTest uses simple visual tasks. Even so, the shared conclusion substantively corroborates the earlier work. All the sources predate the post, and none shows the reverse.

attribution.note: Marcus's own quip, right after he quotes the study.

semantics.note: The punchline is rhetorical, but it firmly says the models in the study are not AGI. Treating it as an observation is defensible.

contract.note: Marcus gave no definition of AGI. The contract's plain reading (broad human-level competence, flaws allowed) is ordinary and not stretched either way.

evidence.note: Levels of AGI framework (2024) surveys AGI definitions; does not evaluate the 2026 model versions.

reviews.rationale: The packet holds only one item, a definitional framework, which is context. No evaluation of the studied model versions against broad human-level competence was found, either for or against. The contract says isolated visual failures are not enough on their own, so the packet does not settle the claim.
